_about: Hand-written HTML lessons and pages for this subject. Each lesson is lessons/<file>.html (the header and article only; the site adds navigation, contents and the pager). Pages in pages/<file>.html get the site header and nothing else. Links inside them are written from the site root, like /machine-learning/02-gradient-descent/.

lessons.title: Linear regression
lessons.blurb: Squared error, the normal equations, least squares as projection, and the Gaussian maximum-likelihood view.

lessons.title: Gradient descent and the delta rule
lessons.blurb: Gradients, steepest descent, the delta rule, and why the learning rate must stay below 2 over the largest curvature.

lessons.title: Logistic regression and log-loss
lessons.blurb: Sigmoid and log-odds, Bernoulli likelihood, cross-entropy, its gradient and Hessian, and separable data.

lessons.title: Generalisation
lessons.blurb: Expected vs empirical risk, the bias–variance decomposition derived, the exact train–test gap for least squares, and cross-validation.

lessons.title: Regularisation
lessons.blurb: Ridge in closed form and through the SVD, penalties as priors (MAP), the lasso and soft thresholding, weight decay and early stopping.

lessons.title: Softmax regression and cross-entropy
lessons.blurb: K classes with one logit each, the cross-entropy loss and its p − y gradient, entropy and KL, log-sum-exp, temperature.

lessons.title: Stochastic optimisation
lessons.blurb: Minibatch gradients and their variance, the SGD noise floor derived, momentum's square-root speed-up, Adam and AdamW, warm-up and cosine schedules.

lessons.title: Evaluating classifiers
lessons.blurb: Confusion matrices, base rates and Bayes' rule, ROC and AUC as a probability, precision–recall, cost-based thresholds, calibration and Platt scaling.

lessons.title: Linear algebra for ML: eigenvectors, SVD and PCA
lessons.blurb: The spectral theorem, the SVD built from scratch, Eckart–Young, the pseudo-inverse, PCA as constrained maximisation, power iteration.

lessons.title: Probability for ML: expectation, Gaussians, MLE and MAP
lessons.blurb: Expectation and variance rules, total expectation and variance, Gaussian conditioning proved, maximum likelihood, Beta–Bernoulli MAP, LLN and CLT.

lessons.title: Information theory: entropy, cross-entropy and KL
lessons.blurb: Surprise and entropy, source coding and Huffman codes, Gibbs' inequality, forward vs reverse KL, mutual information, perplexity.

lessons.title: Optimisation: convexity, constraints and Lagrange multipliers
lessons.blurb: Convexity and why it makes optimisation easy, the linear convergence proof for gradient descent, Lagrange multipliers, maximum entropy gives softmax, KKT.

lessons.title: Problem set: stage 2
lessons.blurb: Twenty problems with worked solutions on generalisation, regularisation, softmax, stochastic optimisation and evaluation.

lessons.title: Assignment: linear models from scratch
lessons.blurb: Implement least squares, gradient descent, logistic regression, ridge, lasso and cross-validation; an autograder checks each one.

lessons.title: Matrix calculus
lessons.blurb: Gradients by the differential-and-trace method, worked examples up to the Gaussian covariance MLE, vector–Jacobian products, gradient checking.

lessons.title: Decision trees
lessons.blurb: Greedy splitting, Gini and entropy and why strict concavity matters, fast split search, regression trees, cost-complexity pruning.

lessons.title: Bagging and random forests
lessons.blurb: The variance of a correlated average, the bootstrap and out-of-bag error, random feature subsets to decorrelate trees, majority votes, feature importance.

lessons.title: Gradient boosting
lessons.blurb: Fit each new tree to the gradient of the loss: functional gradient descent, the Newton step and gain formula behind XGBoost, and why small learning rates win.

lessons.title: Problem set: stage 3
lessons.blurb: Twenty problems with worked solutions on split criteria, pruning, bagging, random forests and gradient boosting.

lessons.title: Assignment: gradient-boosted trees from scratch
lessons.blurb: Build a small XGBoost: losses, exact split search, second-order trees, subsampling, early stopping and permutation importance; an autograder checks each part.

lessons.title: Neurons and the multilayer perceptron
lessons.blurb: Stack neurons with a nonlinearity: what a hidden layer does to space, why ReLU networks are piecewise linear, a proof of universal approximation, and why depth still matters.

lessons.title: Backpropagation
lessons.blurb: The chain rule run backwards: computational graphs, why reverse mode is cheap, the backward rule for every layer, memory and checkpointing, and an autodiff engine in 60 lines.

lessons.title: Training deep networks
lessons.blurb: Keep signals and gradients at the right scale: He and Xavier initialisation derived, normalisation layers, dropout and weight decay, and a recipe for getting a network to train.

lessons.title: Problem set: stage 4
lessons.blurb: Nineteen problems with worked solutions on what networks can represent, backpropagation, initialisation, normalisation and dropout.

lessons.title: Assignment: an autograd engine and an MLP on MNIST
lessons.blurb: Build a small tensor autograd library with layers, dropout, SGD and AdamW, then train an MLP on MNIST to over 98%; an autograder checks each part.

lessons.title: Convolutional networks
lessons.blurb: Share one small filter across every position: convolution defined precisely, equivariance proved, size and receptive-field arithmetic, the backward pass, and im2col.

lessons.title: Recurrent networks
lessons.blurb: One cell applied through time: backpropagation through time, why gradients vanish or explode, and the LSTM's additive memory that fixes it.

lessons.title: Modern CNNs and residual networks
lessons.blurb: LeNet to AlexNet to VGG to ResNet: the degradation problem, why skip connections let gradients reach every layer, bottlenecks, and transfer learning.

lessons.title: Word embeddings
lessons.blurb: Meaning as geometry: PMI and the SVD, word2vec's skip-gram with negative sampling, the proof that they factorise the same matrix, and where analogies come from.

lessons.title: Attention
lessons.blurb: A soft dictionary lookup: scaled dot-product attention, why the scores are divided by the square root of d, masking, symmetries and cost, and a head that solves associative recall.

lessons.title: The Transformer
lessons.blurb: Multi-head self-attention, MLPs, residuals and layer norm; positions from sinusoids to RoPE; the causal mask; 12d² parameters and 6N FLOPs per token; a GPT in NumPy that learns to reverse sequences.

lessons.title: Vision transformers and contrastive learning
lessons.blurb: Images as sequences of patches; CLIP's contrastive loss, its mutual-information bound and temperature; zero-shot classification; a toy CLIP trained from scratch.

lessons.title: Problem set: stage 5
lessons.blurb: Twenty-one problems with worked solutions on convolutions, residual scaling, RNN gradients, embeddings, linear attention, KV caches, positions, and contrastive temperature.

lessons.title: Autoencoders and variational autoencoders
lessons.blurb: Latent-variable models, the ELBO derived two ways, the Gaussian KL, the reparameterisation trick against the score-function estimator, and a VAE whose latent space discovers a bar's angle and length.

lessons.title: Generative adversarial networks
lessons.blurb: The minimax game, the optimal discriminator and the Jensen-Shannon divergence, saturating gradients, mode collapse and the Wasserstein distance; a GAN with hand-written gradients on eight Gaussians.

lessons.title: Assignment: a residual network in NumPy
lessons.blurb: Convolution by im2col and its adjoint, max pooling, batch norm with running statistics, residual blocks and augmentation, with an autograder; then a ResNet on MNIST to 99.2%.

lessons.title: Diffusion models
lessons.blurb: The forward noising process and its closed-form marginals, the posterior of one reverse step, the ELBO that becomes 'predict the noise', and a DDPM trained from scratch that samples a spiral out of noise.

pages.title: Watch it learn
pages.idea: A line fitting itself, four learning rates in the same bowl, and logistic regression bending into an S-curve.
